To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) subsidence and sequence-stratigraphic analyses are complementary and (2) tectonics and thermal subsidence are the main factors controlling the evolution of the Cretaceus carbonate platforms in the Prebetic.

(i) the Cretaceous carbonates and clastic successions of the Prebétic (Jumilla–Yeclla Region) are divided into 12 sequence sets, which can be subdividied into several third order sequences and their constituent systems tracts; (ii) the tectonic and sedimentary evolution of the southern continental margin during the Cretaceous was strongly controlled by the opening of the Bay of Bizcay, the Iberia-Africa divergence,

the tectonics of the Iberia-Africa convergence and the evolution of the North Atlantic and the Bay of Bicay controlled the subsidence and sequence development in the Jumila-Yecla region during the Cretaceous.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a regional study of a carbonate platform, where the subsidence analysis was performed in the framework of sequence stratigraphy and the evolution of the platform is explained by the interplay of tectonics and sea-level changes.

the integration of the subsidence and sequence-stratigraphic analysis of a carbonate platform in order to explain the accommodation changes controlling the evolution of the carbonate platforms of the Jumillay–Yecla Region.
the integration of sequence stratigraphic and subsidence analysis to explain the tectonic evolution of the continental margin of the southern Iberian Peninsula during the Cretaceous.

the Cretaceous shallow-marine successions of the study area were controlled by the combined action of the tectonics and thermal subsidence.

the integration of subsidence and stratigraphic analyses is a powerful tool for understanding the tectonostratigraphic evolution of a given area.
